readings.title: The label that asked a question
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A local museum displayed an ordinary lunch box from a former factory. Its first label listed the date, material and donor. Few visitors paused. A new label began by asking where workers ate when there was no canteen. It then used the box to introduce the short meal breaks and shared outdoor spaces of that period. Visitors spent longer at the case and discussed their own workplace meals. The facts about the object had not changed. What changed was the connection between those facts and a recognisable human question. The curator kept the original catalogue details available in a separate record.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：细节、推断、词义与主旨

readings.title: The route visitors chose
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: An exhibition designer arranged five rooms in a historical sequence. She expected everyone to begin with the earliest period. During opening week, visitors often entered the brightest room first and moved in several directions. Rather than forcing them back to the planned route, the team added short context panels at each entrance. A complete timeline remained near the centre for people who wanted an overview. Visitors could now understand a room without having seen all the others. The designer learned that a coherent exhibition could support different journeys if each part offered enough orientation.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：细节、推断、词义与主旨

readings.title: The borrowed cup
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: For an exhibition about migration, a resident lent a cup carried during a move many years earlier. The museum wanted to show it beside an enlarged family photograph. The lender agreed to display the cup but was uncertain about making the photograph public. Staff initially saw the two items as one story. After further conversation, they separated the permissions and used a simple map instead of the photograph. The display still communicated the journey without exposing relatives who had not participated in the decision. The experience reminded the team that a compelling interpretation does not remove a contributor's right to set limits.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：细节、推断、词义与主旨

readings.title: A trial with empty frames
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: Before buying screens for a new gallery, staff taped paper rectangles to the walls at proposed heights. They invited adults of different heights, including seated visitors, to read sample text inside the rectangles. Several screens would have been too high, and one would have reflected a bright window. Adjusting paper cost almost nothing. The team changed the placement before ordering mounts and wiring. The temporary display looked unfinished, but that was part of its usefulness: participants felt comfortable suggesting changes. A rough model made decisions visible while they were still inexpensive to revise.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：细节、推断、词义与主旨

translation.stem:
Translate this original passage into Chinese.

An exhibition helps people notice relationships that may not be obvious when objects stand alone. The words beside an object can invite curiosity or close it down. Clear language does not require a simple history with every difficulty removed. It can introduce uncertainty honestly and encourage visitors to consider why different people remember the same event in different ways.
translation.referenceAnswer: 展览帮助人们注意到物件单独陈列时不明显的关系。物件旁边的文字既能激发好奇，也可能使好奇止步。清晰的语言并不要求把历史简化到抹去所有复杂之处。它可以诚实地呈现不确定性，并鼓励参观者思考不同的人为何以不同方式记住同一事件。
translation.explanation: 参考译文展示一种可接受的表达；保留原文信息及逻辑、中文通顺的其他译法同样有效。

writing.stem:
Write about 120 English words for this original simulation task.

Your learning centre will display objects showing changes in everyday life. Propose one object, explain the story it could tell, and suggest an accessible way to present it.
writing.sampleAnswer: I would display a paper bus ticket beside a photograph of a modern payment screen. The ticket could introduce changes in how people prepare for journeys and ask for help. A short label might describe buying a ticket from a conductor and invite visitors to compare that experience with paying by phone. The display should avoid suggesting that everyone welcomes the same change. Some travellers appreciate speed, while others value speaking to a person. Large print and a recorded version of the label would support different visitors. A clearly marked replica ticket could be handled. Finally, a small comment board could collect memories and practical difficulties, making the display a conversation about daily travel.
writing.explanation: 范文用于作答后参考；观点与例子可以不同，但须回应全部要求并表达清楚。
